name: Tracking Outcomes
title: Tracking Outcomes
answer: Tracking outcomes means a school uses a reporting service to learn whether its graduates enrolled in college and whether they stayed enrolled. The National Student Clearinghouse provides this service for $595 per high school per year. The point is to see whether counseling and preparation are working for all groups of students, not just to collect data.

sections.body: Tracking outcomes is the practice of following what happens to graduates after they leave high school. It solves the problem of schools having good intentions but no feedback about whether their counseling and academic preparation actually helped students in college. By seeing enrollment and persistence rates, a district can tell whether its efforts are paying off. Looking at outcomes by group also shows whether all students are being served well. This turns intentions into a basis for improvement.
sections.heading: The idea

sections.body: In practice, a high school or district can subscribe to the National Student Clearinghouse service, which reports which graduates enrolled in college and whether they persisted, at $595 per high school per year. School leaders and counselors review the results in aggregate and by group. If many graduates enroll but do not return for a second year, the school might strengthen preparation or connect students with support at their colleges. If some groups enroll at lower rates, the school can look for barriers. The supplied text does not give separate grade band examples, so the practice is described at the high school and district level.
sections.heading: How it works in school

sections.body: The text gives no evidence label, study, or research finding for tracking outcomes. It states only that the National Student Clearinghouse offers a service that reports which graduates enrolled in college and whether they persisted, for $595 per high school per year. It also states that districts can use this data to see whether counseling efforts are paying off and that outcomes by group show whether all students are being served well. On the supplied text, this idea rests on practice rather than research.
sections.heading: What the evidence says

sections.body: Outcome data is personal information and must be handled carefully. Reports should be reviewed in aggregate, not used to single out individual students. The same privacy rules that apply to all student data apply here. Counselors can use the data to improve programs without exposing any student. The text leaves program improvement decisions to counselors, within the same privacy rules that apply to all student data.
